name: @blobatar/react-native
description: React Native and Expo adapter for blobatar — deterministic geometric avatars.
//sideEffects: No `*.css` entry, unlike every other adapter. Those carry one so a bundler cannot drop `import "blobatar/motion.css"`; there is no motion layer on this platform and no stylesheet to protect, so the field would be guarding nothing.

scripts.//prepack: See the same note in `packages/react/package.json`. It matters more here than anywhere: this package's first release cannot go out through `release.yml` at all — npm will not register a trusted publisher for a name that does not exist yet — so its very first publish is a manual one, which is precisely the run with no turbo ordering in front of it.

//peerDependencies: `blobatar` is pinned to an exact major for the reason `packages/react/package.json` spells out: under ADR-0008 the major names the generation, so a mixed pair is the wrong picture rather than a version skew, and `packages/harness` asserts the range rather than trusting release tooling with it. The three React Native peers are the opposite case and take ranges: `react-native-svg`'s majors are its own, not blobatar's generations, so a caret is correct there. The floors are the New Architecture's — it is the only architecture current React Native has, and a lower floor would be a configuration nobody here can test and everybody would be asked to support.
//devDependencies: `react-native` is here for types only and never loads. `SvgProps` extends `ViewProps`, so `react-native-svg`'s declarations reach into `react-native` and `tsc` needs it on disk — but that package's own entry point is Flow-typed source Bun cannot parse, which is why `packages/harness` renders this adapter through a stub rather than the real components. See the header of its `test/react-native-stub.ts`.
author: Alain
//check: No `bun run build` here. The build is a turbo task that `check` depends on, so it runs once for the whole workspace before any check reads a `dist` — a check that rebuilt its own package would delete `dist` out from under a concurrent check in another one.
